newsitem.title: USA: Golden Books to cut 200 jobs; reports loss.
newsitem.headline: Golden Books to cut 200 jobs; reports loss.

text.p: Golden Books Family Entertainment Inc. said Thursday it would cut 200 jobs, or about 10 percent of its work force, and sell a manufacturing plant in Racine, Wis. as part of an ongoing restructuring.
The New York-based children's book publisher also reported a narrower loss for the third quarter.
The company said it would move its manufacturing to a new, more efficient plant in Racine and farm some of its printing work out to other companies.

It said it also reached agreements with five unions on a package of wage and benefit concessions and work rule changes and won $5 million in tax credits and low-cost financing from state and local authorities related to the move to the new plant.
"We are working aggressively to restore Golden Books to profitability and to grow the business," said Philip Rowley, chief operating officer of the Golden Books Publishing Co.

Golden Books Family Entertainment reported a net loss of $15.5 million, or 73 cents a share, in the quarter ended on Nov. 2, compared with a net loss of $37.5 million, or $1.79 a share, in the 1995 quarter. A year ago the company was known as Western Publishing Group Inc.
It cited stiff competition in children's books and electronic storybooks in particular, limited new product introductions, price cuts and falling international sales.
Total sales fell 15 percent to $89.5 million from $105.2 million.
"We are well along in our efforts to overhaul our production and supply chain, which will reduce costs, improve quality and increase efficiency," Chairman Richard Snyder said in a statement.
"These efforts, which are laying the groundwork for long-term revenue growth and profitability, are not apparent in our third quarter results, and will not impact the business until 1997."
He said additional restructuring steps would be announced during the fourth quarter. The company had about 2,025 employees at the end of the quarter.
The company said it will hire an outside company to manage its information systems, and was negotiating with Computer Sciences Corp., a leading data systems management company.
It said it will maintain its two distribution facilities in Coffeyville, Kan., and Crawfordsville, Ind., for now.
Golden Books stock fell 75 cents to $11.25 on Nasdaq.
